log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Whimsicott

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blaziken. Lead Whimsicott + Gengar: turn one Whimsicott fires Prankster Tailwind (self-side, unaffected by Armor Tail) while Gengar Taunts Farigiraf's slot to deny Trick Room (non-priority bypasses Armor Tail); Focus Sash guarantees Tailwind through Make It Rain. Kingambit switches in free vs Gholdengo/Farigiraf (double-resists Gholdengo STABs, immune to Psychic) and cleans with Sucker Punch once Armor Tail leaves; Mega Blaziken under Tailwind outspeeds their whole roster and brea
decisions.notebook: Durable matchup facts vs this opponent: (1) Kingambit double-resists Gholdengo STABs (Steel 0.5x, Ghost 0.5x), is immune to Psychic, and Kowtow Cleave is 2x SE on both Gholdengo and Farigiraf — it is the safe pivot for both. (2) Armor Tail blocks my Prankster Encore AND Sucker Punch while Farigiraf is on the field; Gengar's non-priority Taunt is the Trick Room answer, and Whimsicott's self-side Tailwind is unaffected. (3) Gholdengo Shadow Ball guaranteed OHKOs Gengar; Gengar's Shadow Ball is only a possible OHKO back (86-155%) — never trade the 1v1, pivot to Kingambit. (4) Close Combat is only 1x vs Farigiraf (Psychic resists Fighting); kill it with Kowtow Cleave instead. (5) Mega Blaziken Flare Blitz likely OHKOs Corviknight (base-forme calc already 74-128%); the rest of my team barely dents Corviknight (Gengar Sludge Bomb is immune, Moonblast/Energy Ball resisted) — preserve Blaziken when Corviknight is in their four. (6) Rotom-W Will-O-Wisp threatens all four of my physical attackers; answer it with Gengar/Whimsicott special pressure — Kingambit resists both Rotom STABs but fears burn. (7) Their speed control is Corviknight Tailwind and Farigiraf Trick Room; under my Tailwind, Mega Blaziken/Excadrill/Gyarados outspeed their entire roster (max 138 Rotom-W). Game 1 plan: Whimsicott+Gengar lead, Kingambit+Mega Blaziken back.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf + Gholdengo lead: Armor Tail blocks all priority (Prankster Encore, Sucker Punch), Good as Gold blocks status (Taunt). Turn 1 Trick Room reverses speed vs Tailwind teams. Gholdengo Make It Rain threatens Whimsicott, Shadow Ball threatens Gengar. Backline Azumarill + Mudsdale thrive under TR: Huge Power Liquidation hits Blaziken/Excadrill/Kingambit, Stamina Body Press cleans up. Mudsdale Ground immunity with Levitate Rotom if needed, but Azumarill+Mudsdale cover the physical sweep.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Blaziken (Speed Boost), Prankster Tailwind Whimsicott, Kingambit (Sucker Punch blocked by Armor Tail), Life Orb Gengar, Mold Breaker Excadrill, Intimidate Gyarados (Wacan Berry). My Armor Tail blocks all their priority. Good as Gold blocks Taunt/Encore/Thunder Wave. Trick Room is the speed solution. Mudsdale's Stamina counters physical spam. Azumarill Liquidation threatens Blaziken/Excadrill/Kingambit/Gyarados. Keep Gholdengo healthy for Make It Rain spam. Protect to scout for turn 1 double-target.

decisions.rationale: Armor Tail blocks Prankster Encore but not Gengar's natural Taunt, and Taunt (162 Spe) lands before Farigiraf's -7 Trick Room. Tailwind is Prankster priority, so it is up before Gholdengo acts; sash guarantees Whimsicott survives Make It Rain. If Gholdengo Shadow Balls, Gengar trades itself for 3 turns of no Trick Room plus Tailwind — then Kingambit enters, double-resists Gholdengo, is immune to Farigiraf's Psychic, and at 140 effective Speed outspeeds and 2x SE Kowtow Cleaves both foes. decisions.rationale: Gengar is the safe pivot: it resists Farigiraf's Dazzling Gleam and Kingambit is guaranteed to move before Gholdengo, with Kowtow Cleave dealing 84.5-150.6% — usually removing the Shadow Ball threat before it fires. Worst cases are fine: Gholdengo Protect just wastes its turn, Farigiraf Protect still leaves it slower than Kingambit under Tailwind next turn, and a low-roll survivor Gholdengo is finished by Kingambit next turn even if it KOs Gengar.

Mudsdale EQ is a guaranteed OHKO on Gengar (113-134%) even with spread reduction, while Azumarill Protects through Gengar's Sludge Bomb. This eliminates the main threat and pressures Kingambit (44-52%) without risking Azumarill. Tailwind leaves Gengar faster, but Protect blocks its attack regardless.
decisions.notebook: Gengar's Sludge Bomb OHKOs Azumarill (128-151% Life Orb). Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave (47-56% base) + Supreme Overlord (1.1x) threatens Mudsdale but Stamina boosts Defense after each hit. Mudsdale's Earthquake OHKOs Gengar (113-134%) and damages Kingambit (44-52%) as spread. Protect + Earthquake is the safest play to eliminate Gengar immediately. Opponent has Excadrill (Mold Breaker, SoftSand), Gyarados (Intimidate, Wacan), Blaziken (Speed Boost, Mega) in back. Trick Room remains my win condition when available.

decisions.rationale: Mudsdale's Earthquake is a guaranteed OHKO on Gengar, so it must faint or Protect this turn. Both my attackers outspeed under Tailwind; Shadow Ball (38-70%) plus Kowtow Cleave (~25-44% after the Stamina +1 Def) KOs Mudsdale most of the time. If it Protects, Azumarill's hit is survivable and Gengar (162) still outspeeds both foes after Tailwind ends, with Blaziken in reserve for the 3v2. Splitting damage risks a free EQ.

Game 1 plan executed: Kingambit cleaned Gholdengo/Farigiraf under Tailwind; same lead framework is sound for game 2.

Every other option concedes to Body Press with certainty; this is the only line that keeps any win chance against the opponent's most likely play.

Reconsider bringing/Megaing Blaziken unless Corviknight is likely; answer Azumarill with Gengar Sludge Bomb or Kingambit Iron Head, and if Gengar must be sacked to Earthquake, do it deliberately to Cursed-Body-disable EQ.

reflections.summary: Won because Mudsdale's Stamina boosts allowed it to absorb multiple hits from Gengar and Kingambit, then Earthquake KOed Gengar and crippled Kingambit. Azumarill finished Blaziken and Kingambit. The opponent's aggressive double-targeting left them with only two mons, which were outsped and outbulked after the user's switch-in.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, anticipate opponent may bring Excadrill (Mold Breaker ignores Stamina) or Gyarados (Intimidate). Consider leading with Azumarill and Mudsdale to pressure early, or use Trick Room setup with Farigiraf to counter speed. Protect Mudsdale from potential Taunt/Encore and beware Kingambit's Supreme Overlord boost if more faints.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendency: aggressive lead with Whimsicott + Gengar, Tailwind, then double target. Gengar (Life Orb, Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Dazzling Gleam, Taunt), Kingambit (Kowtow Cleave, Sucker Punch, Iron Head, Protect), Whimsicott (Tailwind, Moonblast, Energy Ball, Encore), Blaziken-Mega (Flare Blitz, Close Combat, Swords Dance, Protect). Not brought: Excadrill (Mold Breaker, SoftSand), Gyarados (Intimidate, WacanBerry). Future: Opponent may switch leads or bring Excadrill/Gyarados. Key: Mudsdale's Stamina is strong but vulnerable to Mold Breaker. Azumarill's Liquidation crucially hits Blaziken and Kingambit. Avoid using Earthquake if Disabled or if it could hit allies. Use Protect to scout. Endgame: Kingambit with Supreme Overlord is dangerous; finish with priority or strong moves.
